title: Photography
tagline: From camera obscura to smartphone cameras.

events.title: The first photograph
events.text: Nicéphore Niépce produces “View from the Window at Le Gras”, the earliest surviving photograph, on a pewter plate.

events.title: The daguerreotype is revealed
events.text: Daguerre’s process (and Fox Talbot’s calotype around the same time) gives the public a practical way to make permanent images.

events.title: Kodak: photography for everyone
events.text: George Eastman’s Kodak camera popularises roll film and the slogan “You press the button, we do the rest”.

references.label: History of the Kodak camera — Kodak

events.title: Kodachrome brings colour
events.text: Kodachrome, the iconic colour film, is introduced, giving everyday photographers rich, archival colour.

events.title: The first digital camera
events.text: Steven Sasson at Eastman Kodak builds the first self-contained digital camera — a 0.01 megapixel prototype.

references.label: First digital camera — Crafted at Kodak

events.title: The camera phone
events.text: Sharp’s J-SH04, sold in Japan, popularises the integrated camera phone, foreshadowing the universal camera.

events.title: The smartphone camera
events.text: The iPhone (and Android successors) put a capable camera plus instant sharing in every pocket, ending the point-and-shoot era.

references.label: The rise of the smartphone camera
